clue.text: Where classified information is open to alll

definitions.text: Where classified information is open to alll

blocks.note: surface reading: secret intelligence, as in an official leak
setter's reading: classified means sorted into catalogue categories, and these buildings let anyone walk in

explanation.surface: Someone complains that state secrets have been thrown open to everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: Classified sounds like top secret, but here it means arranged by subject on the shelves, as books in PUBLIC LIBRARIES are.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal book collections catalogue their stock by subject and admit any member of the community free of charge.

clue.text: A broken set of unusual pieces way back

indicators.note: going back means the word for a road is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: odd means strange or unusual
chess or draughts pieces are called men
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A collector describes an incomplete set of strange pieces found down a back lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces as men is a board-game convention; ST turned round gives TS at the end of ODDMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover odds and ends, the remnants of an incomplete collection that no longer forms a whole.

indicators.note: irregular is read as odd, so the features wanted are the odd-numbered characters of the name

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the name Bernice

explanation.surface: A rather unkind remark about the uneven features of a woman called Bernice.
explanation.walkthrough: Irregular features sounds like an unflattering face, but irregular means odd, and the odd letters of Bernice are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white edible rind, named after a region east of Paris.

clue.text: He is not yet a master of martial arts

definitions.text: He is not yet a master of martial arts

blocks.note: surface reading: someone still training in karate or judo
setter's reading: the degree below a Master of Arts, held by a man who is also not yet married, punning martial on marital

explanation.surface: A student of kung fu has not yet reached the rank of master.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses combine: a Bachelor of Arts has not yet taken the Master's degree, and a bachelor has not yet entered the marital state.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor holds the first university degree, below a Master's, and is also an unmarried man.

clue.text: Smooth when applied to a leg

indicators.note: applied means attached, so the short words are stuck on the end of the limb word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that a lotion or wax leaves the skin smooth once rubbed on a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase to a is applied to leg by tacking it on behind, giving LEG + A + TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the musical direction for playing notes smoothly and connected, without breaks between them.

blocks.note: surface reading: the first move of a chess game or a negotiation
setter's reading: a device that rings so that someone will come and open the front door

explanation.surface: Something that announces the first gambit in a game or campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the button by the entrance rings a chime telling the household to come and let the visitor in.

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to enjoy greatly
second meaning: a tangy condiment or pickle that whets the appetite

explanation.walkthrough: Like looks like a preposition meaning similar to, but it is the verb to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for taking great pleasure in something and a noun for a savoury pickle served with food.

blocks.note: surface reading: pennyroyal is a small herb of the mint family, so a gardener tending it
setter's reading: the official in charge of making coins, pennies with the monarch's head on them

explanation.surface: A gardener is put in charge of a patch of the herb pennyroyal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pennyroyal is a kind of mint; split as penny-royal it becomes the royal coinage, overseen by the head of the Royal Mint.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the historic title of the officer who ran the Royal Mint, responsible for producing the nation's coinage.

indicators.note: a burlesque is a mocking parody, so the following words are travestied into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether performing nude in a striptease show is really what is happening, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlesque reads as the strip-show genre, which suits naked, but it is the signal to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake a task is to commit oneself to it or set about doing it.

clue.text: The last of the home games

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A sports fan talks about the final fixture of the season played at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence a byword for the end of anything.

clue.text: City doctor with the shuffling kind of walk

indicators.note: shuffling mixes things up, so the letters of the little word beside it are rearranged

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
taken as written

explanation.surface: A town doctor who walks with a shuffling gait.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling seems to describe the doctor's walk, but it rearranges the. The Lambeth Walk is a jaunty Cockney song and dance from the 1937 musical Me and My Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth names a famous strutting Cockney dance step, so it is one particular sort of stroll.

clue.text: Did it save Berlin from musical plaigarism?

definitions.text: Did it save Berlin from musical plaigarism?

blocks.note: surface reading: the songwriter Irving Berlin protected from people stealing his tunes
setter's reading: the 1948-49 Allied operation that flew supplies into the blockaded city, read playfully as the lifting of a tune

explanation.surface: A question about whether something protected the composer Irving Berlin from having his songs copied.
explanation.walkthrough: An air is a melody, and to lift is to steal, so the word punningly means tune theft; really it is the Berlin Airlift, when Allied planes supplied West Berlin during the Soviet blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic operation transported food and fuel by plane to West Berlin, keeping the city going through the blockade.

indicators.note: arranged suggests putting things in a new order, as a musician reworks a score

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of music that was once scored for the cornet.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical context makes cornet the brass instrument, but in Britain a cornet is also an ice-cream cone.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a cornet is the wafer holder for ice cream, which is the same thing as a cone.

blocks.note: first meaning: completely, entirely
second meaning: the nude state, as in the idiom in the ...

explanation.surface: A body that is completely naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means totally, and the noun appears in the informal idiom 'in the altogether', meaning without any clothes.

clue.text: Aloof like Gower, say, with three out

indicators.note: three out tells us that a trio of characters at the front is dropped

blocks.note: the Gower is a peninsula in south Wales, so it is an example of something peninsular

explanation.surface: Someone stand-offish is compared to Gower, perhaps the cricketer, with three batsmen dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gower suggests the England batsman David Gower and out suggests cricket, but here it is the Welsh peninsula; PENINSULAR loses PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes a narrow, inward-looking outlook, keeping apart from others like an island cut off by sea.

indicators.note: playing suggests frolicking about, so the preceding letters move around freely

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hundred people who keep losing are taking part in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks used to catch and throw a ball into a goal.

blocks.note: oil is drawn from a well
off means halted or cancelled, as a switched-off pump

explanation.surface: A wealthy oil field that has been capped.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a capped oil well and being well off do not literally mean the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably off means having plenty of money, so this is a synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: One who has grounds for his lack of sagacity?

definitions.text: One who has grounds for his lack of sagacity?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who has good reasons for being foolish
setter's reading: land measured in acres, so the word splits as a sage plus a field

explanation.surface: A person who has some justification for being foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Grounds means land as well as reasons; the word seems to describe a wise landholder but actually means a know-all who only thinks himself clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a smart alec who pretends to knowledge, so the apparent wisdom is really its absence.

clue.text: Pirate company misbehaving at La Scala, perhaps?

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so these letters do not stay in line

blocks.note: taken as written
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A troupe performing The Pirates of Penzance runs riot at the Milan opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala is the famous opera house in Milan; perhaps marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: What happens on the stage of that great Milan house is grand musical drama, the kind of performance this adjective describes.

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen in a heap, so the castaway's name is jumbled
after tells us the jumbled name is placed behind the word for a run

blocks.note: a race is a run against others
taken as written

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe falls exhausted after going for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Here points back to the whole clue: the place where a run is held, as a race on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is the track or ground where horse races are run, so it is the place indicated.

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so one character is trimmed from the mushroom word
rolled suggests tumbling over, so the remaining letters turn into a new order

blocks.note: agarics are mushrooms, taken as written

explanation.surface: Cigarettes made from chopped-up mushrooms rolled into papers.
explanation.walkthrough: One A is chopped from AGARICS, leaving GARICS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokes is informal for anything smoked, and cigars are rolled tobacco leaves smoked for pleasure.

blocks.note: un is French for a
a parachute is carried folded in a pack on the back

explanation.surface: An instruction to open a French-made parachute.
explanation.walkthrough: Parachute stands for PACK, the bundle in which the canopy is folded and worn.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpack a suitcase or box is to open it and take out its contents.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in a spot of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: Engaged sounds like betrothed or in combat, but it is the mechanical sense of gears locking together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth mesh when they interlock, which is what engineers mean when gears engage.

clue.text: Stir up Roger! Pull yourselves together

indicators.note: to stir is to mix around, so the following letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to rouse Roger, then an order for the whole team to compose themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir up reads as one phrasal verb, but only stir is the signal; up joins the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To regroup is to reorganise after a setback, an order to rally and recover composure together.

blocks.note: first meaning: to greet with enthusiastic applause
second meaning: an old sense of a shout of applause, like the cheering at a Roman triumph

explanation.surface: Greeting a once-famous Triumph car or motorcycle with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumph suggests the British car and motorcycle maker; once marks an old-fashioned sense of the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hail with praise, and the old noun meant a public burst of cheering such as greeted a victor.

indicators.note: holding means the steersman word wraps round the little word inside it

blocks.note: a cox steers a rowing boat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boat's steersman cradling a pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet looks like a noun for an animal, but it is a verb meaning to fondle or humour.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to cajole gently with flattery and caresses, much as one pets and pampers someone.

clue.text: Nobles who hold court in London venue

blocks.note: surface reading: aristocrats receiving visitors in state
setter's reading: these peers come before court in the name of a big London exhibition hall

explanation.surface: Aristocrats receive admirers at a London venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a large exhibition centre in west London, so these nobles literally hold the word Court after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are members of the British peerage ranking above viscounts and below marquesses.

clue.text: Somehow RA can dash into colour

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the academy's letters and the next word are mixed
to dash is to smash, so the following little word is broken up and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written; RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Royal Academy painter manages to dash some paint onto the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: Into looks like a link to colour, but it is fodder: two separate shuffles give CARNA and TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnation is a pinkish flesh tint, named after the flower and used by painters for skin tones.
